reviews.evidence: Declared "MIT AND OFL-1.1": the package code is MIT and the Inter font files are OFL-1.1. The fonts ship as separate font files the app loads, kept under OFL-1.1 and not relicensed; OFL-1.1 permits bundling with any software, and the FSF lists it as a free licence for fonts. The OFL text and Inter's copyright notice ship with the release (component asset:inter-font).

Observed 2026-11-18 at 6b31a7cc: absent from the release JS bundle. `expo export --platform android --no-bytecode --source-maps` built index-6eb99dbb.js, and its source map's 9,911 sources come from 68 npm packages, none of them this one. No Gradle project or native library comes from it either. A Node-only build dependency, reached in the lockfile only through @expo/cli, @expo/config, @expo/config-plugins, @expo/fingerprint, @expo/metro-config and expo-updates (only expo-updates/utils/build/vcs.js, a command-line helper). Wave's releases don't convey a copy of it, so its BlueOak-1.0.0 terms don't reach them.

components.evidence: Ported 2026-10-13 (a3f085e9) from Metrolist's app/src/main/kotlin/com/metrolist/music/utils/potoken/{PoTokenGenerator,PoTokenWebView,JavaScriptUtil}.kt and app/src/main/assets/po_token.html. The port didn't record an upstream revision. Metrolist v13.7.0 (7c5ba3ad22cb562d337897f82163a2b7fce665f3, the last release before the port) holds those paths; its po_token.html is identical to Wave's below Wave's 3-line header (upstream last changed in 98116669); its LICENSE is the GPLv3 text and neither it nor the README states "or any later version"; the ported files carry no headers. NewPipe v0.29.3 (8e15d04e) has the originals under app/src/main/java/org/schabi/newpipe/util/potoken and its README grants GPL-3.0-or-later. Every reading allows GPLv3, so the code can be part of a GPL-3.0-only work; the owner can't relicense it. Resolved 2026-11-18: v13.7.0 is recorded as the revision the port follows (the html matches it), and each file names Metrolist's and NewPipe's source paths, revisions, copyright holders and licences. Each file's header says it was modified by Wave, from which date, and that it is conveyed under the GNU GPL version 3 (GPLv3 section 5a).
components.notice: Metrolist contributors and NewPipe contributors, GPL-3.0 (NewPipe: GPL-3.0-or-later); modified by Wave from 2026-10-13. Headers in each file.

components.evidence: Their doc comments say the response walk "follows" Metrolist's page classes (GPL-3.0), innertubex's AccountMenuResponse (GPL-3.0) or ytmusicapi (MIT), and YtClient reuses Metrolist's search filter parameters. No comparison against an upstream revision was made, so whether expression was copied is open. Compatibility doesn't depend on it: GPL-3.0 and MIT code can both be part of a GPL-3.0-only work. Resolved 2026-11-18: the files credit Metrolist, innertubex and ytmusicapi as derived code, with each upstream's licence and copyright holder; the upstream revision isn't recorded and the headers say so. Each file's header says it was modified by Wave, from which date, and that it is conveyed under the GNU GPL version 3 (GPLv3 section 5a).

components.evidence: Ported 2026-10-28 (0504b9bc) from shazamio-core tag 2.0.0 (5690a2e99ba2aa6456a742c5b1defd8e7841826b): LICENSE "MIT License, Copyright (c) 2024 dotX12", Cargo.toml license = "MIT". Wave's comment calls the generator "itself SongRec's"; SongRec 0.8.2 (79d3d771) has src/core/fingerprinting/{algorithm,hanning,signature_format}.rs, Cargo.toml license = "GPL-3.0+", and shazamio-core's THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md doesn't name SongRec. Open rights question: whether shazamio-core's files derive from SongRec. Compatible either way, as MIT and GPL-3.0-or-later both allow GPL-3.0-only. Resolved 2026-11-18: both files carry shazamio-core's MIT notice and credit SongRec (GPL-3.0-or-later), since no comparison has shown shazamio-core's code independent. Each file's header says it was modified by Wave, from which date, and that it is conveyed under the GNU GPL version 3 (GPLv3 section 5a).

The POM names the "Android Software Development Kit License". androidx.credentials:credentials-play-services-auth:1.6.0 also brings com.google.android.gms play-services-auth 21.1.1, play-services-identity-credentials 16.0.0-alpha08, play-services-auth-blockstore 16.4.0 and play-services-fido 21.0.0, all under that licence (their POMs). These ship inside the APK, beside third-party GPL-3.0 code (innertubex, the Metrolist/NewPipe ports). They aren't part of the phone's operating system, so whether the GPLv3 System Library exception covers them is unresolved, and the owner can add a section 7 permission only for code the owner holds. Owner exception, 2026-11-18: the owner keeps googleid 1.2.1 and the Play services libraries it and credentials-play-services-auth bring (10 under the Android SDK License, listed in android-release-closure.json), and NOTICE.md grants a GPLv3 section 7 additional permission to convey the owner's code combined with them. That permission covers only code the owner holds. The third-party GPL code in the same APK (innertubex, quackjs, the Metrolist/NewPipe ports) has no such permission from its holders; the owner accepts that risk, as every release so far has shipped this combination.
components.notice: Google Play services and Google ID libraries, Android Software Development Kit License; conveyed under the section 7 additional permission in NOTICE.md.

components.evidence: Observed 2026-11-18 at 6b31a7cc: after prebuild, `./gradlew :app:dependencies --configuration releaseRuntimeClasspath` resolves 274 libraries and 22 Gradle projects, recorded with each POM's licence in docs/licensing/android-release-closure.json. Libraries: 194 Apache-2.0; 57 MIT (hermes-android, react-android, slf4j-api and others); 6 Glide artifacts under BSD-2-Clause and Apache-2.0; avif BSD-2-Clause; bolts-tasks 1.4.0 BSD-3-Clause (Fresco's dependency; its repository also carries Facebook's Additional Grant of Patent Rights v2, a patent grant that adds no condition to the copyright licence and that the FSF list doesn't classify); jaudiotagger LGPL-2.1-or-later; innertubex GPL-3.0 and quackjs GPL-3.0-only (their own entries); and 10 Play services libraries under the Android SDK License (owner exception, see googleid). Apache-2.0, MIT, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause and LGPL-2.1-or-later are GPLv3-compatible (FSF licence list). The projects are the Expo and React Native modules built from npm packages in npm-packages.json, and Wave's wave-native, wave-glass and kotlin-shared. Native code inside npm packages (react-native-skia-android 154.0.0's Skia build, Hermes) declares only its package's licence, MIT for both. The record holds for this commit: a change to a build.gradle, or to the npm packages that bring Gradle modules, needs the closure observed again.

Every v* release tag from v0.5.0 (the first) to v0.68.0-ti contains a3f085e9, which added innertubex and the Metrolist/NewPipe ports. Those APKs, OTA bundles and repacks were conveyed without a licence for the combined work, a notices file or source access tied to each release. The repository at each tag is public, which alone isn't a compliance finding. Owner exception, 2026-11-18: the owner declares GPL-3.0-only (LICENSE, NOTICE.md) and accepts the risk for the third-party GPL code those releases conveyed without notices or per-release source access; that has been the status quo of every release. The owner turns on RELEASE_SOURCE_DELIVERY and backfills source access for the published releases as docs/release-source.md describes (legacy manifests for the releases before the gate); GPLv3 section 8 reinstates rights once a violation is cured.
